title: Customer proxy session sync failure — postmortem & runbook draft
content:
Summary:

On 2026-06-14 ~03:12 UTC a subset of customers running the Private control-plane behind an L7 customer proxy started reporting elevated 502/504 errors and sporadic control-plane disconnects for agent-based control-plane tunnels. The incident lasted approximately 2h 40m for affected customers; our routed control plane remained available but telemetry showed repeated tunnel re-establishment attempts, increased latency, and request timeouts for long-lived sessions.

Impact:
- ~6 customers (private deployments) observed control-plane agent reconnect loops and intermittent API errors for admin operations.
- Some on-prem inference endpoints experienced elevated latency and a small number of failed streaming sessions.
- No data loss reported, but customer-facing availability and SLA markers were impacted.

High-level cause hypothesis (short):
The customer-side L7 proxy (transparent reverse proxy / DPI appliance) had an aggressive session timeout and performed asymmetric connection teardown during TCP keepalive windows, which led to connection tracking (conntrack) entries becoming stale on the customer NAT appliance. The Redwood proxy-agent expects long-lived TCP/WebSocket sessions to persist; when the appliance silently dropped the backend state, the proxy-agent attempted to re-establish tunnels. Compounding the issue, the customer's firewall performed TCP sequence sanitization which occasionally caused packets to be dropped rather than reset, producing half-open connections and confusing on-prem conntrack tables.

Timeline (reconstructed from logs + slack + customer packet captures):
- 2026-06-14 02:58 UTC: First alert from internal probe: spike in websocket reconnects for tenant-42.
- 2026-06-14 03:12 UTC: Customer support ticket created (SRE-4682). Customer-side NOC reports increased 502s from control-plane REST endpoints.
- 03:16 UTC: Oncall triage — grep of proxy-agent metrics shows jump in agent reconnects and an increase in RST counts on server side.
- 03:24 UTC: Customer shares tcpdump from their edge proxy (snip). Analysis shows server-to-client packets with no matching conntrack entry on the appliance after a 15s idle period.
- 03:40 UTC: We deploy short-term mitigation (adjusted agent keepalive frequency for affected tenant to 10s) to reduce chance of silent teardown. Immediate partial reduction in reconnect attempts.
- 04:10 UTC: Customer disables DPI mode on their proxy appliance; reconnects stop escalating.
- 05:50 UTC: Confirmed stabilization. Post-incident checks scheduled.

Root causes (detailed):
1) Customer L7 proxy idle/session timeout shorter than Redwood agent expectations. Some appliances silently drop backend connections without signaling RST, leaving our agent believing socket remains open.
2) Conntrack/NAT state mismatch on customer's appliance when backend connections were torn down silently, leading to packets from server hitting stateful firewall with no mapping, causing apparent asymmetric drops and extra SYN/ACK/FIN churn.
3) DPI/tcp-sequence normalization on appliance caused packet modifications that resulted in occasional in-flight packet drops rather than proper teardown signals.
4) Lack of proactive detection in our telemetry for silent teardown patterns (we tracked reconnect rates but not in-proxy conntrack mismatch signals).

What went well:
- Customer NOC provided timely tcpdump and configuration dump which allowed us to correlate packet-level discrepancies.
- Quick temporary tweak to keepalive frequency reduced exposure while customer adjusted config.
- Runbook for websocket reconnect detection correctly surfaced the issue to the right teams.

Contributing factors (lessons):
- Our default keepalive/timeout assumptions are optimistic for many on-prem proxies. We need better heuristics or configuration knobs for private deployments.
- We did not have an automated probe that checks for silent connection teardown (a test that injects pings and expects RST/FIN within a window).
- Documentation for customers about recommended proxy settings (idle timeouts, conntrack settings, DPI behavior) is incomplete and not surfaced during Private onboarding.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Temporary agent config change for affected tenants: keepalive interval lowered to 10s and aggressive reconnect backoff disabled for 30m window.
- Advice to customer NOC: disable DPI/tcp-normalization mode and increase backend session timeout to >=180s (customer applied 300s).
- Added targeted alert: detect >5 reconnects/min per-agent for >2 minutes (hotfix).

Permanent actions & follow-ups (owners and ETA):
- SRE (Marcus Nguyen) - Add a "silent-teardown" detection in proxy-agent telemetry (create metric: agent_conn_state_mismatch_count) and alerting. ETA: 2026-07-01.
- Product Docs (Leah O'Connor) - Publish "Private deployment networking guide" with recommended proxy/firewall settings including conntrack, NAT, DPI, and keepalive recommendations. ETA: 2026-07-10.
- Proxy-Agent (Diego Ramos) - Implement configurable keepalive profiles and ability to enable aggressive probing when behind suspected intermediaries; include opt-in on onboarding UI. ETA: 2026-07-08. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy-agent/pull/731.
- SRE/Oncall - Add synthetic probe to detect silent-teardown patterns (end-to-end probe that validates session state and expects explicit teardown signals). Owner: eng-sre. ETA: 2026-07-05.
- Sales/Customer Success - Update onboarding checklist to require confirmation of customer-side proxy behavior for all Private deployments. Owner: customer-success. ETA: 2026-06-30.

Runbook draft: (steps for oncall when similar symptoms appear)
1) Triage and confirm scope
   - Check agent reconnect metric: agent_reconnects_total by tenant and agent_id.
   - Cross-check internal control-plane latency graphs and request error rate.
   - Open incident ticket and notify customer-success to contact customer NOC for tcpdump.
2) Quick probes to run
   - Run tcpdump on control-plane ingress (if hosted path): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <customer-edge-ip> and look for FIN/RST behavior after idle windows.
   - On agent side (if reachable): sudo ss -ntp | grep <agent_pid> and examine ESTAB entries and Tx/Rx counters.
   - Check server kernel logs (dmesg) for conntrack or nf_conntrack warnings: sudo dmesg | grep -i conntrack
   - Query proxy-agent metrics: curl http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep agent_conn
3) Short-term mitigations (apply with caution)
   - If customer agrees, reduce agent keepalive to 10s and force probe interval: kubectl patch configmap proxy-agent --patch '{"data":{"keepalive_interval":"10s"}}' (example — use tenant-specific config in Private).
   - Ask customer to temporarily disable DPI/tcp-normalization on the L7 appliance and increase backend session timeout.
   - If NAT/conntrack exhaustion suspected, instruct customer to increase nf_conntrack_max and lower timeout for RELATED tracking if appropriate.
4) Escalation path
   - If mttr > 30m and customer still affected, escalate to oncall-2 and network platform. Provide packet captures and annotated timeline.

Monitoring changes (planned):
- New metric: agent_conn_state_mismatch_count (see follow-up).
- Alert: "agent reconnect storm" threshold lowered to 5 reconnects/min with per-tenant dedup window and runbook link.
- Dashboard: add long-lived session health panel showing median session duration and distribution by tenant.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we default to more aggressive keepalive for all Private customers? Tradeoff: higher chattiness increases token-unit costs and noise. Proposal: make aggressive probing opt-in at onboarding + enable automatic heuristics when reconnect patterns detected.
- Can we improve agent-side recovery to probe with an explicit RST if a connection appears half-open? (security implications).
- Determine whether we can detect DPI-related packet modifications by comparing sequence/ack patterns across server vs client captures.

Notes-to-self / working fragments:
- Customer appliance: vendor: AcmeProxy v8.2.1 — their default DPI sets backend idle TTL to 60s.
- tcpdump snippet shows S->C payload continuing but ACKs from C dropped; supports silent backend-teardown hypothesis.
- Potential follow-up experiment: spin up a controlled AcmeProxy instance in CI, run long-lived websocket, and simulate DPI-mode to reproduce failure.

Appendix: Helpful commands & queries
- Check agent reconnects: curl "https://metrics.redwood/metrics?query=agent_reconnects_total{tenant="TENANT"}"
- Kernel conntrack table: sudo conntrack -L | grep <customer-host> | wc -l
- Packet capture (example): sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/edge.pcap host <edge-ip> and then analyze with Wireshark to look for missing FIN/RST after idle period.

Contact log:
- 03:18 UTC: A. Patel -> customer-noc (email) requesting tcpdump and proxy config.
- 03:50 UTC: Customer NOC confirms they disabled DPI and increased timeout.
- 05:55 UTC: Post-stabilization check-in with customer and close incident.

Draft status: This is a working postmortem and runbook sketch. Please add corrections, packet excerpts, and any customer config snippets to the Confluence doc (linked above).

References: see linked_artifacts list; ticket SRE-4682 contains raw tcpdumps and customer config export.
